chapter: Billie Holiday and the band's singers
title: How the Teddy Wilson sessions drew on whichever band was in town
summary: Hinton explains that the personnel came from the stars of whatever band was in New York, and Jones cites the January 30, 1939 session.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Hey, Jo, I might be able to answer that question in a little bit. At that time, Bill, as Jo said, 1937, I was in the Cotton Club with Cab. I came for the first time in 1936 and Jo was with Basie, they came into town in 1936. John Kirby's band was in town. Duke Ellington was around sometime between '36 and '37. The way that orchestras were picked for the band, Teddy Wilson had been picked as the leader, as you see by the first date that you did, right, Jo? Teddy Wilson had been picked as the leader. He was used as the so-called name, one of the so-called stalwarts, of whatever band happened to be in town. If Duke's band was in town they would be using Johnny Hodges. You name whoever stellar guys were in Duke's band, in Teddy Wilson's band to record, because Teddy Wilson had the contract. He was the leader. They would use guys from Duke's band. If Benny Goodman happened to be in town, we would use Allen Reuss or Charlie Christian or Gene Krupa. We'd mix it up. If Cab happened to be in town we'd use Cozy and perhaps on the strength of Cozy, who I'm sure you remember, I got into

the thing, on the strength of the recommendation that Jo and Cozy, as being a pretty good guy in the bass section, they would use me. Now if Basie was in town they would use Jo Jones and Walter Page. If John Kirby's band happened to be in town at that time, and John Kirby certainly had seniority over me at that particular time, then John Kirby would be the bass player. So this is why the discography reads with all these different guys.

Because you remember, Bill, since you're here, you were stationary. Milt had a position because after he left from Cab they were booked for a year and H! Six months in New York and six on the road. they had gone and entered a different category. A Now I have to jump from '37 to come to 1939, January 30. Now whose on the date? Teddy Wilson and his orchestra. But look who's on the date? Roy Eldridge, Bennie Carter. Bennie had just come back from Europe. Ernie Powell. Teddy Wilson on piano. Danny Barker on bass. Milt Hinton, Cozy Cole, and Billie Holiday. You see?

That's right, January the 30th, 1939, see, because you remember at that time I told you that we had been to the Famous Door and that's when Cozy joined Cab, 'cause we were there thirty 5 1/2 months. We were on 52nd Street.
